title: Internal Hom preserves finite Tor amplitude by dévissage
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $A$ a
finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, and $X$ a scheme of finite type over
$k$. For $K,L\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$, the internal Hom
$R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)$ lies in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$.

Here $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ denotes the full subcategory of the ordinary derived category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ on the small étale site consisting of bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in some interval $[a,b]$, $a\leq b$, against every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. The internal Hom is the ambient derived internal Hom of the ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. No separatedness assumption on $X$ or presentation of $A$ as a quotient of a discrete valuation ring is imposed.

proof.text: We prove the assertion simultaneously for all pairs of objects on each finite-type $k$-scheme, by Noetherian induction on reduced closed subsets of a fixed $X$. The field spectrum is Noetherian (a field has only two ideals); hence $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The minimal-closed-subset principle [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] justifies induction on proper closed subsets. Give each such subset its reduced induced closed structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; it is still finite type over $k$, since affine coordinate rings are quotients of finite-type $k$-algebras. Use the original, possibly nonreduced $X$ for the top case and the reduced induced closed schemes for its strict descendants. A closed subset of a descendant is closed in $X$, and the two reduced induced structures agree by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The inductive hypothesis is the conclusion for every pair in $\Dctf(Z_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ for every such proper closed subscheme $Z$. On the empty scheme all module sheaves are zero, so the conclusion holds.

We record the closure and inverse-image facts used throughout the induction. Clause (3) of [det-sf-flat-model-generation], with its explicit ordinary étale constant-$A$ convention, says that $\Dctf$ is closed under shifts, cones, retracts and isomorphisms; in particular it has the two-out-of-three property in distinguished triangles. For every scheme considered here, [thm-constructible-serre] supplies closure of constructible $A$-module sheaves under kernels, cokernels and extensions; zero and isomorphism invariance follow from the definition. Thus the explicit weak-Serre hypothesis of the main-20261015 statement of [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] holds throughout the proof. Finite direct sums are constructible by the split exact sequences, and retracts are constructible as kernels of $1-e$ for an idempotent $e$. For every morphism between the Noetherian schemes at issue, inverse image preserves $\Dctf$: choose a bounded flat constructible representative by [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], apply the exact inverse image of constant-$A$ modules [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] termwise, and use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] for flatness and [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback] for constructibility of the underlying sheaf of sets. They are constructible as $A$-module sheaves: on each pulled-back stratum, after trivializing the finite set sheaf, the finitely many addition and scalar maps are locally constant, so a finite refinement of the covering makes the restriction constant as an $A$-module sheaf (as in Step 4). The resulting complex is bounded in the same degrees. Its bounded constructible cohomology follows by the stupid filtration and [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory], and the converse direction of [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] gives the Tor bound. In particular this applies to $j^*$ and $i^*$ below.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1 and 3: flat models, inverse image, and triangulated closure

proof.text: For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, direct image also preserves $\Dctf$ in this setting. Indeed [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] identifies $(i_*F)_{\bar x}$ with $F_{\bar z}$ at a point on $Z$; outside $Z$ it is zero by [lem-kun-04ca]. These formulas, exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and their conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] show that $i_*$ on module sheaves is exact. They also show it preserves flatness: by [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar], tensoring a short exact sequence with $i_*F$ has stalkwise the tensor sequence with the flat $A$-module $F_{\bar z}$ on $Z$, and the zero sequence off $Z$. Here flatness of $F_{\bar z}$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] applied to the geometric point of the topos, whose inverse image is the stalk. Exactness is detected by applying the exact conservative stalks to kernels and cokernels. By [lem-fin-closed-immersion] $i_*$ preserves constructibility. Applying $i_*$ termwise to a bounded flat constructible model therefore gives another such model; [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] and [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] put its derived object in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: exact closed direct image carries flat constructible models to such models

proof.text: Assume $X$ is nonempty. Choose bounded flat constructible models $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ for $K,L$ using [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], with supports $[c,e]$ and $[a,b]$. Apply [prop-constructible-generic-constancy] to each of the finitely many nonzero $P^q$, and intersect the resulting dense opens. This gives a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ on which all $P^q$ are finite locally constant. The local trivializations can be chosen $A$-linear: after trivializing the finite underlying set sheaf, the finitely many addition and scalar-action maps are locally constant, so refine finitely many times. Clause (1) of [det-sf-flat-model-generation] says the stalks of each flat constructible $P^q$ are finite projective $A$-modules. Thus étale locally on $U$ each of the finitely many $P^q$ is a direct summand of a finite free constant-$A$ sheaf, simultaneously on the covering family of finite fibre products over $U$ of members of the individual trivializing covers; the family covers because each geometric point lifts through each of the finitely many covers. The complement has the reduced structure $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ from Step 1 and is a proper closed subset. Every open of a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; thus $U$ is quasi-compact and finite type over $k$ (on affine charts the quasi-compact open is covered by finitely many principal opens).

source.place: Proof, Step 1: the good dense open

proof.text: On $U$, form the ordinary sheaf Hom complex $H^\bullet=\mathcal Hom_A^\bullet(P^\bullet|_U,Q^\bullet|_U)$ and its canonical map to the Hom complex into a K-injective resolution of $Q^\bullet|_U$. On each member $V$ of the étale covering of Step 4 on which the finitely many $P^q$ are direct summands of finite free constant sheaves, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] identifies the restriction of that map with the canonical quasi-isomorphism computing derived internal Hom on the slice; the lower bound on $Q$ and upper bound on $P$ are exactly its hypotheses. Derived internal Hom commutes with these slice restrictions by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], so the map is a quasi-isomorphism globally: the cohomology sheaves of its cone vanish on a covering, hence vanish. For each degree pair $(q,r)$, apply [lem-sfb-lisse-split-hom-flat-constructible] on the Noetherian scheme $U$ (Step 4) with $E=P^q|_U$, which is a direct summand of a finite free constant sheaf on each member of the covering of Step 4, and $G=Q^r|_U$, which is flat and constructible as the inverse image of a flat constructible sheaf along the open immersion $j$ (Step 2): $\mathcal Hom_A(P^q|_U,Q^r|_U)$ is flat and constructible. Finite direct sums of flat constructible sheaves are constructible by Step 2 and flat since tensor product distributes over finite sums. Thus $H^n=\bigoplus_q\mathcal Hom(P^q,Q^{q+n})$ (a finite sum) is flat constructible, and it is zero unless some $q$ satisfies $c\leq q\leq e$ and $a\leq q+n\leq b$, i.e. outside $[a-e,b-c]$. Bounded constructibility of the cohomology follows from [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] by the finite stupid filtration, and the flat-model equivalence [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] (interval $[a-e,b-c]$, nonempty since $a\leq b$, $c\leq e$) yields $R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*K,j^*L)\in\Dctf(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: local Hom calculation and bounded flat constructible representative

proof.text: The functor $Rj_*$ sends every $C\in\Dctf(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ into $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. Constructibility and boundedness follow from [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients]: the finite ring $A$ is killed by a power of $\ell$, an integer invertible in $k$. By [lem-kun-0f10] choose a finite integer $d\geq\operatorname{cd}(j)$. Clause (2) of [det-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-open-tor] then takes any Tor interval $[v,w]$ for $C$ to $[v,w+d]$ for $Rj_*C$, against all étale module sheaves. The fields, coefficients and finite-type hypotheses in that statement agree with ours; no separatedness of $X$ is required. We use only its étale clause (2).

source.place: Proof, Step 2: constructibility and Tor bound for open direct image

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] to the open immersion $s=j$, for which the factorization is the identity closed immersion followed by $j$ and hence $Rs^!=j^*$. It gives $R\mathcal Hom_A(j_!j^*K,L)\cong Rj_*R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*K,j^*L)$. The inner object is in $\Dctf(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ by Step 5 and its direct image is in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ by Step 6. This proves the open outer term needed for gluing, without an internal-Hom pullback assertion for a closed immersion.

source.place: Proof, end of Step 2: open ambient-Hom identity

proof.text: The ambient support triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] gives $i_*Ri^!L\to L\to Rj_*j^*L\to$. Here $j^*L\in\Dctf(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ by Step 2, so $Rj_*j^*L$ is in $\Dctf$ by Step 6. Two-out-of-three from Step 2 gives $i_*Ri^!L\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. Applying $i^*$ and using $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ from [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful] gives $Ri^!L\in\Dctf(Z_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. This counit extends degreewise to the derived categories because both inverse image and closed direct image are exact, as established in Steps 2 and 3. Also $i^*K\in\Dctf(Z_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ by Step 2.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: derive finite Tor amplitude of the exceptional restriction from the support triangle

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] to $s=i$, with identity open factor. The isomorphism is $R\mathcal Hom_A(i_*i^*K,L)\cong i_*R\mathcal Hom_A(i^*K,Ri^!L)$; ordinary $i_*$ agrees with its derived functor by Step 3. The two inputs on $Z$ are in $\Dctf$ by Step 8. Since $Z$ is a proper reduced closed subscheme, the inductive hypothesis applies and puts their internal Hom in $\Dctf(Z_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. Step 3 puts its direct image in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. This proves the closed outer term; it uses no preservation theorem for $Ri^!$ beyond what Step 8 just proved.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: closed ambient-Hom identity and induction

proof.text: Use [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] on the bounded object $K$ to obtain $j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to$. By [lem-sf-hom-triangulated], applying $R\mathcal Hom_A(-,L)$ gives the distinguished triangle $R\mathcal Hom_A(i_*i^*K,L)\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)\to R\mathcal Hom_A(j_!j^*K,L)\to$. Its first and third terms are in $\Dctf$ by Steps 9 and 7. The two-out-of-three property established in Step 2 gives the desired conclusion for the middle term, completing the induction.

split_report.summary: Retained the full arbitrary finite commutative ell-primary coefficient ring and nonseparated finite-type scheme statement. Expanded the Noetherian induction into ten steps with existing general étale flat models, explicit closed-pushforward flatness, local split-projective Hom calculation, separate open-image bounds, ambient support triangle, and gluing. Replaced coefficient-restricted imported citations and created no new nodes.
